beats.vo: First, you need to understand the chaos of Mecca. The year is 610 AD.
This barren valley is never truly quiet. It's the Wall Street of the ancient desert.
Caravans come and go. Bringing fine fabrics from Yemen. Rich oils from the Levant.
Pilgrims flock from every corner of Arabia to circle the Kaaba.
A sacred house they believe was built by Abraham and his son, Ishmael.
But the faith of Abraham is dead. The Kaaba is now surrounded by hundreds of stone idols.
Every tribe has its own god. They swear by Al-Lat. They sacrifice to Al-Uzza.
Then, they go right back to the market to cheat each other.
The strong crush the weak. Daughters are buried alive because they are seen as a disgrace.
Wealth is the only measure of a man's worth.
But in the middle of this noisy, corrupt city, there is one man who cannot find peace.
He is nearly forty years old. An orphan since childhood.
Raised by his grandfather, then his uncle.
Now, he is comfortable. He is married to Khadijah, a wealthy, highly respected businesswoman.
The people of Mecca love him. They don't call him by his name. They call him Al-Amin.
The Trustworthy.
His name is Muhammad, the son of Abdullah.
He never bows to the idols. He refuses to eat their sacrifices.
But he also doesn't know what he should worship.
He just knows the world is broken. And he craves something he can't even name.
That craving pushes him out of the city. Away from the noise.
He climbs a jagged, harsh mountain just a few miles northeast of Mecca. Jabal Nur.
It starts with dreams. His wife, Aisha, would later recount how it all began.
She said before the revelation, he started having dreams that were as clear as the breaking dawn.
Whatever he saw in his sleep, happened exactly like that in real life.
Driven by these visions, he seeks total isolation.
He finds a tiny cave near the mountain's peak. Cave Hira.
It's barely big enough to sit or lie down.
But from the mouth of this cave, if the sky is clear, he can see Mecca far below.
He stays here for days. Practicing Tahannuth, deep reflection and worship.
He brings basic provisions. Water. Dates.
When he runs out, he walks all the way down, goes back to Khadijah, resupplies, and climbs right back up.
Some historians say he did this for an entire month every year.
What is he thinking about up there? The records don't say.
We can only imagine a man sitting in deafening silence.
Looking for the meaning behind the sky, the earth, and his own existence.
And pay attention to Khadijah here. This is crucial.
She doesn't stop him. She doesn't complain that he disappears into the mountains for days.
She packs his bags. She waits. She lets him go.
This silent, unwavering loyalty is about to become his only lifeline.
Because the night that changes everything has finally arrived.
It is the month of Ramadan. Muhammad is alone in the cave.
Suddenly, the truth he was searching for doesn't just appear. It grabs him.
A majestic, terrifying entity, an angel, manifests in the tiny space.
The entity gives one commanding order: "Read!"
Muhammad is paralyzed. He replies, "I am not a reader."
Immediately, the angel violently grabs him. Squeezing him so tight he feels his bones might crack.
He is suffocating. Pushed to the absolute limit of human endurance.
Then, the angel releases him. Muhammad gasps for air.
But the entity commands again: "Read!"
Terrified, Muhammad gives the exact same answer. "I am not a reader."
The angel grabs him a second time. The grip is just as crushing.
He is released again. "Read!" the angel commands a third time.
He answers again. The angel squeezes him for the third time. He is utterly exhausted. Completely broken down.
Then, the angel releases him one last time and speaks the five verses that will change the world.
"Read in the name of your Lord who created."
"Created man from a clinging substance."
"Read, and your Lord is the most Generous."
"Who taught by the pen."
"Taught man that which he knew not."
Only five verses. No rules about prayer. No laws. No stories of past prophets.
Just five verses. But this is the match that lights a 23-year fire of revelation.
The angel vanishes. The cave is empty again.
Muhammad is alone. But he is terrified. His heart is pounding out of his chest.
He scrambles down the treacherous mountain in the dead of night.
He bursts through the door of his home, screaming for his wife.
"Cover me! Cover me!"
Khadijah rushes to him. She wraps him in heavy blankets until his violent shivering stops.
He tells her everything. The cave. The squeezing. The voice.
He looks at her in absolute despair and says, "I fear for my life."
Put yourself in Khadijah's shoes. Your husband comes home shaking, talking about a monster in a cave.
You'd panic, right? You'd think he lost his mind.
But what she says next is one of the most powerful psychological anchors in human history.
She doesn't talk about ghosts. She doesn't talk about magic.
She talks about his character.
"Never!" she says. "By God, God will never disgrace you."
She lists the receipts: "You keep good relations with your family."
"You help the poor and the destitute."
"You serve your guests generously."
"You assist those hit by calamities."
She is saying: The universe is just. A man who lives a life this pure cannot be destroyed by God.
Before anyone else believed, before there was any proof, Khadijah believed.
But Khadijah knows they need an expert. Someone who understands the supernatural.
Remember the blind old man we mentioned at the start? It's time to meet him.
His name is Waraqah bin Naufal. Khadijah's own cousin.
In a city of idol worshippers, Waraqah is a unicorn.
He abandoned idolatry years ago. He became a Christian. He translates the Gospel into Hebrew.
Khadijah brings Muhammad to him. "Listen to your nephew," she says.
Muhammad tells the story. Waraqah listens in absolute silence.
Then, the old man speaks. And his words change the trajectory of Muhammad's life forever.
"That is the Namus," Waraqah says. "The Keeper of Secrets. The same Angel that came to Moses."
He just confirmed it. Muhammad is not crazy. He is a Prophet.
But before the relief can settle in, Waraqah drops a massive, devastating prophecy.
"I wish I were young," the old man whispers. "I wish I could be alive when your people kick you out."
Muhammad is stunned. He is Al-Amin! The most loved man in the city!
"Will they really drive me out?" he asks in disbelief.
"Yes," Waraqah replies coldly. "No man has ever brought what you brought without being treated as an enemy."
"If I am alive on that day, I will support you with all my strength."
It is a dark, terrifying promise of war, exile, and suffering.
Muhammad braces himself for what comes next. He waits for the angel to return. He waits for the instructions.
And then... nothing.
Days pass. Waraqah dies.
Weeks pass. The angel doesn't come back. The sky is completely silent.
Muhammad is left entirely alone, doubting everything all over again.
This agonizing silence is known as the Fatrah.
How long did the silence last? Did God abandon him?
The answer comes in the second revelation, and it is brutally intense.
It transforms him from a quiet thinker in a cave into a fearless warner of the masses.
Want to know what that second revelation was? You have to watch the next episode right here.
